app.title: fielddash: dashboards for field survey responses, built from the form schema
app.summary: A person picks a survey project, and the dashboard loads the form and its responses, either from a field-collection service or from local files. They narrow the responses with sidebar filters, each one chosen to suit the question's type. Then they look over the overview: response counts, a map of where each response was taken, submissions over time and responses per collector. Next they go through every question by section, as charts that can be split by any categorical question, or through a set of pinned charts. Finally they download the filtered responses as CSV or Excel.

task.text: Summarise and keep watch on questionnaire responses while fieldwork is under way, question by question and broken down by group, so they can be shared or analysed further.

data.text: Responses to a structured questionnaire filled in on mobile devices in the field. Each response has typed answers (single choice, multiple choice, number, date, free text, location), a submission time and a collector. A form schema defines the questions, their types, option order and groups.
data.item: one questionnaire response from one interview

stage.text: summarising survey responses while fieldwork is under way, before full analysis

mechanism.text: Sidebar filters, generated from each question's type, narrow the shared set of responses that every page draws from. The Overview page shows counts, a map that switches between points and a heatmap, and a submissions timeline. The Questions page charts each question in section tabs, with a search box, a toggle that hides free-text questions, and a 'Cross with' selector that splits every chart by one categorical question. The Data page shows the filtered table with CSV and Excel downloads.

field.text: descriptive tabulation of household questionnaire surveys collected in the field, in the social sciences

workflow.name: summarise survey responses question by question, filtered and split by group

steps.here: Choose a project from the sidebar selector. The form schema and responses are loaded from the Epicollect5 API or JSON files, matched to each other by stable question refs, and cached. A '↻ Refresh data' button reloads them, and any mismatches between schema and data are listed as warnings.

steps.step: filter to the items that matter
steps.here: Pick questions under 'Add filter'. Each becomes a multi-select, a range slider or a date range, depending on its type. The active filters and 'n of N responses' are shown under the title, and every page uses the filtered responses.

steps.step: look over every item at a glance
steps.here: The Overview page shows responses, collectors, latest entry and the share with a location. Below are a map of survey locations (points with popups, or a heatmap), entries per day, week or month, and responses by collector.

steps.step: compute a value from the data
steps.here: The Questions page charts every question in tabs by form group. Single and multiple choice get bars with count and %, numbers get a distribution with mean and median, and free text gets a table of answers. A search box and a 'Hide open-ended' toggle narrow the list.

'Cross with' turns every chart into stacked bars showing % within each group of the chosen categorical question, or into box plots for numbers. The Highlights page shows pinned pairs of question × group, two per row.

The Data page lists the filtered responses, with multiple-choice answers and coordinates flattened. 'Download CSV' and 'Download Excel' save them, and an expander lists the form's fields with alias, type, column and ref.

distinctive: Charts and filters are generated from the form schema's question types, not from column contents. Questions are identified by stable refs, so adding or reordering questions mid-fieldwork does not break the dashboard.
Multiple-choice questions are counted as % of respondents, so the totals can exceed 100%. Groups beyond eight are folded into 'Other'.
A map of interview locations has a points/heatmap toggle and counts responses that have no coordinates.
Responses per collector and submissions over time let the team track progress during fieldwork.
An optional shared PIN or token gates access, because the responses can contain personal data.
